gloss: to straighten up; to take a serious attitude

definitions.gloss: to straighten oneself up; to resolve to act properly
definitions.explanation: Literally to straighten one's collar: to correct one's attitude and behave with new seriousness, often after a scandal or a reminder of one's responsibilities.

examples.japanese: {襟|えり}を{正|ただ}して⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: I listen with a serious, attentive attitude.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今回|こんかい}→今回：01409_konkai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{不祥事|ふしょうじ}→不祥事：14981_fushouji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧、⟦{社員|しゃいん}→社員：03065_shain⟧⟦{一同|いちどう}→一同：08918_ichidou⟧{襟|えり}を{正|ただ}します。
examples.english: In light of this scandal, all of us at the company will set ourselves straight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{真剣|しんけん}→真剣：01565_shinken⟧な⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{襟|えり}を{正|ただ}さ⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}った→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: Seeing how seriously my senior took the work, I felt I had to straighten up too.

notes:
USAGE:
Common in apologies by companies, politicians and officials ({襟|えり}を{正|ただ}して⟦{職務|しょくむ}→職務：13908_shokumu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{当|あ}たる→当たる：01860_ataru⟧), where it promises better conduct from now on. In personal use it means being moved to act more seriously by someone's example or words.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {襟|えり}を{正|ただ}して⟦{取|と}り{組|く}む→取り組む：04225_torikumu⟧: to tackle something with renewed seriousness
- {改|あらた}めて{襟|えり}を{正|ただ}す: to straighten up once more

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}き{締|し}める→引き締める：15264_hikishimeru⟧: to brace oneself, focus; about concentration rather than moral conduct.
- ⟦{反省|はんせい}する→反省する：21398_hanseisuru⟧: to reflect on one's mistakes.
